fields.value: The paper frames robotic gaze as a behaviour used to select a communicative attention target among multiple people, based on a fuzzy model of human engagement and intent.

quotes.text: To efficiently select an attention target for communication in multi-person interactions, we propose a fuzzy-based classification algorithm which is developed by an incremental learning procedure and which facilitates a multi-dimensional pattern analysis for ambiguous human behaviours.

fields.value: The paper presents an autonomous robot system that estimates people’s engagement from multimodal behaviours and uses a fuzzy model to choose a person to attend to in multiparty interaction. In a three-person test, the robot selected and tracked each participant as an attention target; the model classified attention versus inattention with 86.2% accuracy.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper describes engagement classes and the role of gaze in selecting and tracking an attention target during multiparty interaction, and reports the sensing, model, and robot platform used. It does not report clear measured effects on people or how embodiment influenced the study.
